efet_title: Media Statement: Deli Hummus range Product Safety Recall - The National Consumer Commission
efet_body:
Media Statement: Deli Hummus range Product Safety Recall
Date Posted:
October 3, 2024
On 16 September 2024, Shoprite Checkers notified the Consumer Commission (NCC) of a product recall of the Deli Hummus range manufactured by BM Foods (a member of Sea Harvest Group), following the detection of Listeria Monocytogenes which is a species of foodborne bacteria.
The affected products are the Deli Hummus range, specifically the following:
Traditional Hummus (125g and 300g);
Reduced Fat Hummus (125g);
Zataar Hummus (125g and 300g);
Red Pepper Hummus (125g and 300g); and
Caramelised Onion Hummus (125g).
The respective sell-by dates of the products are 10 September 2024 to 08 October 2024.
Subsequent to the product recall notification, and in line with Section 60 of the Consumer Protection Act 68 of 2008, Shoprite Checkers has now provided an interim Investigation Report to the NCC on the Deli Hummus range. The preliminary findings of the report point to some areas of concern on product handling at the manufacturing level, however, the NCC awaits a final report from Shoprite Checkers. Parallel to the said in-house processes, the NCC is independently investigating the recalled products on identified operational issues that pertain to food safety.
The NCC’s Acting Commissioner, Mr. Hardin Ratshisusu, urged consumers to immediately stop consuming the products and return same to the supplier for a full refund with or without any proof of purchase. He further added that “at this stage, the NCC is not able to determine the extent of the distribution of the products as this is the subject of an investigation. Suppliers are urged not to distribute these products further until the investigation is finalised.”
The NCC is monitoring this recall based on the Product Recall provisions of the Consumer Protection Action read with the product recall safety guidelines.
ENDS
Issued by: National Consumer Commission (NCC)

efet_body:
Product Recall: Consumers urged to return certain Mercedes-Benz
vehicles Date Posted: June 10, 2022 Product Recall: Consumers are urged to return certain Mercedes-Benz vehicles. The National Consumer Commission (NCC) urges consumers who are in possession of Mercedes-Benz ML, GL, (model series 164) and R-Class (model series 251) to stop driving these vehicles and contact Mercedes-Benz for further assistance. To contact The National Consumer Commission about this and other Product Recalls , you can use any of the channels that can be found on our Contact page. news_title: Product safety recall – Audi Q3, Hyundai Santa Fe MX5 HEV and Toyota Hino 700 trucks - The National Consumer Commission (NCC)
efet_title: Product safety recall - Audi Q3, Hyundai Santa Fe MX5 HEV and Toyota Hino 700 trucks - The National Consumer Commission
efet_body:
Product safety recall – Audi Q3, Hyundai Santa Fe MX5 HEV and Toyota Hino 700 trucks
Date Posted:
October 8, 2026
The National Consumer Commission (NCC) notifies consumers of three (3) vehicle recalls involving the Audi Q3, Hyundai Santa Fe MX5 HEV and Toyota Hino 700 trucks, as notified by the respective suppliers.
Audi Q3: 235 vehicles
Audi South Africa, a division of Volkswagen Group Africa (Pty) Ltd, has informed the NCC about a recall affecting two hundred and thirty-five (235) Audi Q3 vehicles. The affected vehicles were sold nationally through Audi SA-approved dealers from 16 April 2026 onwards.
Audi SA is recalling these vehicles after identifying a defect with the front seat belts. According to Audi SA, the belt webbing may not have been guided through the metal eyelet on the lap belt tensioner. This means that the seat belt may not be connected to the vehicle’s load-bearing structure. In the event of a fault, the affected seat belt may not restrain the occupant properly.
Hyundai Santa Fe MX5 HEV: 162 vehicles
Hyundai Automotive South Africa has informed the NCC of a recall affecting certain Hyundai Santa Fe MX5 HEV vehicles sold nationally through Hyundai dealerships in 2025. The recall affects one hundred and sixty-two (162) vehicles. The defect concerns the front seat belts, with some vehicles potentially experiencing a misalignment of the front seat belt’s snap-on anchor. This could affect the proper positioning of the front seat belt and may pose a safety risk.
Hino 700 truck tractor series: 482 trucks
Toyota South Africa Motors (Pty) Ltd is recalling Hino 700 trucks sold nationally through the Toyota South Africa dealer network. The recall affects four hundred and eighty-two (482) trucks made available between 17 April 2023 and 17 January 2025.
According to the supplier, the defect is due to a bolt fracture during the assembly process on the production line. As a result, the fifth-wheel coupler securing bolts and mounting plate securing bolts may be fractured. This condition may affect the secure mounting of these components and presents a safety concern.
Consumers who own any of the affected vehicles and trucks are advised to present their vehicles to any dealership for inspection and, where necessary, replacement of the affected component/s. The corrective work will be carried out at no cost to the consumer.
Questions relating to this recall may be directed to:
productrecall@thencc.org.za
.
Ends
